items.stem: Each of the following is associated with the Reagan presidency EXCEPT
options: trickle-down economics
New Federalism
the Whitewater scandal
Star Wars
items.explanation: The Whitewater scandal occurred during the 1990s and involved questionable real-estate dealings by President Clinton. “Trickle-down” theory was Reagan’s economic policy involving corporate tax cuts and New Federalism was his plan to shift federal power to the states. “Star Wars” refers to the Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI), a space-based missile shield program proposed by Reagan as a means of protecting the United States against a nuclear attack by the Soviet Union.

option_explanations.A: Trickle-down (supply-side) economics — cutting taxes, especially corporate taxes, to spur growth — was Reagan's signature economic policy. It is associated with his presidency, so it is not the exception.
option_explanations.B: New Federalism — Reagan's plan to shift power and programs from Washington back to the states — was a hallmark of his presidency. It is not the exception.
option_explanations.C: The Whitewater scandal involved the Clintons' 1990s Arkansas real-estate dealings and belongs to Bill Clinton's presidency, not Reagan's — this is the exception.
option_explanations.D: 'Star Wars' was the nickname for Reagan's 1983 Strategic Defense Initiative, a proposed space-based missile shield against Soviet nuclear attack. It is associated with his presidency, so it is not the exception.

items.stem: Since the end of the Cold War, the continuing American impulse to intervene in the economic and political affairs of other nations around the world is motivated by all of the following EXCEPT
options: fears of renewed Soviet expansion
the protection of human rights
American economic interests
the desire to promote and develop democratic institutions in former communist and Third World nations
items.explanation: Though American relations with Russia remain uneasy, fears of Soviet expansion are a thing of the past; the Soviet Union ceased to exist in 1991, ending the Cold War.

option_explanations.A: The Soviet Union ceased to exist in 1991, ending the Cold War. Fear of renewed Soviet expansion is obsolete and cannot motivate post-Cold War intervention — this is the exception.
option_explanations.B: Protecting human rights has been a stated motive for post-Cold War interventions (e.g., the Balkans, Somalia). It is a real motive, so it is not the exception.
option_explanations.C: American economic interests — markets, resources, trade routes — have continued to motivate intervention after the Cold War. It is a real motive, so it is not the exception.
option_explanations.D: Promoting democratic institutions in former communist and developing nations has been a stated post-Cold War motive. It is a real motive, so it is not the exception.

items.stem: All of the following acts of President Ronald Reagan’s administration are characterized as a return to conservative political values EXCEPT
options: cuts in the federal budget
nominating Sandra Day O'Connor to the Court
tax cuts for corporations
the loosening of government regulation
items.explanation: In 1981, Ronald Reagan, in a move supported by various groups across the political spectrum, made Sandra Day O’Connor the first woman to serve on the Supreme Court. All the other choices represent typically conservative policy decisions by Reagan.

option_explanations.A: Cutting the federal budget was a core conservative Reagan policy — not the exception.
option_explanations.B: Nominating Sandra Day O'Connor in 1981 — the first woman on the Supreme Court — was supported across the political spectrum and was not specifically a conservative ideological move, so it is the exception.
option_explanations.C: Cutting corporate taxes was a core conservative Reagan policy — not the exception.
option_explanations.D: Loosening government regulation of business was a core conservative Reagan policy — not the exception.

items.stem: Which of the following did NOT contribute to the emergence of the New Right of the 1970s and 1980s?
options: The Moral Majority movement
The popularity of Ronald Reagan
The “stagflation” economic condition of the 1970s
A sudden drop in the stock market
items.explanation: Although there was a brief drop in the stock market in 1987 (known as Black Monday), this was not a contributing factor to the emergence of the New Right. All of the other factors did lead to this renewal of conservatism.

option_explanations.A: The Moral Majority, founded by Jerry Falwell in 1979, mobilized evangelical Christians into politics and was a driving force of the New Right — not the exception.
option_explanations.B: Ronald Reagan's popularity embodied and led the New Right's rise — not the exception.
option_explanations.C: The stagflation of the 1970s discredited liberal economic management and fueled the conservative turn — not the exception.
option_explanations.D: The sharp 1987 stock-market drop (Black Monday, October 19, 1987) came after the New Right had already emerged and elected Reagan twice. It did not contribute to the movement's rise — this is the exception.

items.stem: Which of the following happened during the 2000 presidential election?
options: George W. Bush won the popular vote.
Al Gore won the popular vote.
The Supreme Court ordered a recount in Florida, after which Bush was declared the winner.
The media prematurely declared Bush the winner, presumably causing voters who would have voted for Gore not to bother showing up at the polls.
items.explanation: In the 2000 presidential election Al Gore won the popular vote, and many news networks prematurely declared him the winner. However, George W. Bush ultimately won the electoral vote and thus the presidency. Widespread problems with ballot-counting machines in Florida, a swing state with a critical number of electoral votes, caused Gore to refuse to concede the extremely close race for an extended period. The United States Supreme Court ultimately blocked a Florida Supreme Court order requiring a recount and Bush officially won the election.

option_explanations.A: Bush did not win the popular vote. Al Gore won it by about half a million votes nationally.
option_explanations.B: Al Gore won the national popular vote in 2000. Bush won the presidency through the Electoral College after the Florida dispute.
option_explanations.C: The Supreme Court did not order a recount. In Bush v. Gore (2000) it blocked the recount the Florida Supreme Court had ordered, which effectively secured Bush's victory.
option_explanations.D: The networks' premature call went the other way: they first called Florida for Gore, then retracted it. They did not prematurely declare Bush the winner in a way that suppressed Gore voters.

items.stem: In his 1985 State of the Union Address, Ronald Reagan articulated his foreign policy goals in what has come to be known as the Reagan Doctrine. Like Truman, Reagan pledged to
options: support anti-communist resistance movements, particularly in the Third World
sponsor covert military operations to overthrow communist regimes in Eastern Europe
ease tensions between the Soviet Union and the United States
broker a peace agreement between the Palestinians and the Israelis
items.explanation: There are several presidential doctrines you should know for this exam—for example, the Monroe Doctrine and the Truman Doctrine. In most cases, these “doctrines” were delivered as speeches to Congress but became statements of U.S. foreign policy. Alarmed by the establishment of Soviet satellites in Eastern Europe and the potential Soviet threat to Greece and Turkey following World War II, Truman pledged his support to prevent the spread of communism in Europe (although he did not use those exact words). As a cold warrior, Ronald Reagan was committed to providing covert and overt assistance to anti-communist resistance movements, particularly in nations like Afghanistan and Nicaragua.

option_explanations.A: In the Reagan Doctrine (1985 State of the Union), Reagan pledged American support to anti-communist resistance movements in the Third World — the Contras in Nicaragua, the mujahideen in Afghanistan, UNITA in Angola — paralleling Truman's pledge to support peoples resisting communist pressure.
option_explanations.B: The Reagan Doctrine targeted the Third World, not Eastern Europe. Reagan did not sponsor operations to overthrow the Soviet satellite regimes directly.
option_explanations.C: Easing U.S.-Soviet tensions was detente (Nixon and Kissinger), the opposite of Reagan's early confrontational Cold War posture.
option_explanations.D: Brokering Israeli-Palestinian peace was not the Reagan Doctrine. The Camp David Accords were Jimmy Carter's achievement in 1978.

items.stem: During the 1990s, President George H. W. Bush
options: signed the welfare reform bill
persuaded Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin to sign the Camp David Accords
sent troops to fight in the Persian Gulf War
cut taxes and social services
items.explanation: This is a factoid question. President George H. W. Bush led the brief Persian Gulf War in 1990. Choice (B) is Carter, (D) is Reagan, and (A) is President Clinton.

option_explanations.A: The welfare-reform bill (1996) was signed by President Clinton, not George H. W. Bush.
option_explanations.B: The Camp David Accords (1978) were brokered by President Carter with Sadat and Begin, not by George H. W. Bush.
option_explanations.C: George H. W. Bush assembled the international coalition and sent U.S. troops to expel Iraq from Kuwait in the Persian Gulf War (1990-91).
option_explanations.D: Cutting taxes and social services was Reagan's profile. Bush is remembered instead for breaking his 'read my lips' pledge by raising taxes.

items.stem: In the 1990s, the conservative distaste for the changing demographics of the United States fueled
options: the increasing racial and ethnic diversity of the United States
a series of laws mandating bilingual education
laws restricting the employment of undocumented immigrants
increased spending on social services and more ethnic media content
items.explanation: After 40 years of restricted immigration, in the 1960s the federal government threw open the gates to immigrants from around the world. As a result, the United States was flooded with legal immigrants from almost every conceivable nation, which caused cultural conservatives to feel that their country was losing its identity. While conservatives couldn’t restrict legal immigration, they were able to respond by restricting illegal immigration—a much more popular cause, politically. Choice (A) is a cause, not an effect, so eliminate it. Choice (B) is a reversal; bilingual education was abolished in some states, so eliminate that too. Choice (D) confuses causes; if there was more social spending or ethnic media, it certainly wasn’t because of conservative distaste for immigrants. Eliminate (D).

option_explanations.A: Increasing racial and ethnic diversity was the cause of conservative anxiety, not its effect. The question asks what the distaste fueled.
option_explanations.B: This reverses the history. Conservatives opposed bilingual education (e.g., California's Proposition 227 in 1998 abolished it); they did not mandate it.
option_explanations.C: Unable to restrict legal immigration politically, conservatives channeled their response into restricting illegal immigration — employer sanctions and measures like California's Proposition 187 (1994) targeting undocumented immigrants' access to jobs and services.
option_explanations.D: Conservatives pushed to cut social-services spending, not increase it. More spending is the opposite of their position.

items.stem: Which of the following actions by the Clinton administration was most harmonious with Liberal Democrat values?
options: Military peacekeeping interventions in the Balkans and Somalia
Welfare benefit reform to encourage young mothers to reenter the work force
Free trade agreements such as NAFTA and GATT
The effort to pass a universal health care legislation in the Congress
items.explanation: Liberal Democrats would have mixed feelings about war and free trade, so rule out (A) and (C). Welfare benefit reform was in fact designed to get young mothers off welfare, so this was not necessarily a boon to the Democrats. The most ambitious effort by the Clinton administration was to pass a universal health care bill, but this ultimately did not pass Congress.

option_explanations.A: Liberal Democrats have mixed feelings about military interventions, even peacekeeping ones in the Balkans and Somalia — not the most harmonious fit.
option_explanations.B: Welfare reform (1996) was Clinton's centrist 'triangulation' — moving people off assistance and toward work — not a core liberal-Democrat value.
option_explanations.C: Free-trade agreements like NAFTA divided Democrats; organized labor and many liberals opposed them — not the most harmonious fit.
option_explanations.D: The 1993-94 drive for universal health care was the Clinton administration's most ambitious liberal-Democrat undertaking, even though it failed in Congress.

items.stem: The 21st century has thus far seen a dramatic shift in politics characterized by which of the following?
options: A shift in the majority of the American public toward embracing a new conservatism
Deep ideological division and partisan politics between Democrats and Republicans
An increased influence of religion on the policy decisions of the presidential administrations
A decline in public involvement and engagement with Washington politics
items.explanation: The past four elections (2008, 2012, 2016, and 2020) have seen a dramatic shift in political division and partisan politics within the American public. While the new populism associated with Donald Trump and the Republican Party has certainly shaped modern politics, Trump failed to secure a majority of American votes in both 2016 and 2020, making (A) an incorrect answer. Health care, rather than religion, (C), has been a much larger factor in policy decisions thus far in the 21st century and the high voter turnout in the 2020 election suggests a potential shift toward more engagement, in contrast to (D), of the American public in politics.

option_explanations.A: No majority embraced a new conservatism: Donald Trump lost the popular vote in both 2016 and 2020, so a majority shift toward conservatism did not happen.
option_explanations.B: The elections of 2008, 2012, 2016, and 2020 were marked by deepening ideological division and partisan combat between Democrats and Republicans — the defining shift of the century so far.
option_explanations.C: Religion has not been the main driver of 21st-century presidential policy; health care has been the much larger factor.
option_explanations.D: Public engagement did not decline — the 2020 election saw very high voter turnout, suggesting more engagement, not less.

items.stem: For the U.S. military and the national defense industry, the consequences of the September 11 terrorist attacks did NOT include
options: facing further large-scale attacks on U.S. soil
the launch of two prolonged wars in the Middle East
the establishment of the Department of Homeland Security
a series of long-term investigations into the causes of the attack
items.explanation: The September 11 attacks transformed the U.S. military and defense establishment. Investigations, including the 9/11 Commission, examined the causes and funding of the attacks, so eliminate (D). The federal homeland-security apparatus was reorganized with the creation of the Department of Homeland Security in 2002, merging about 22 federal agencies, so eliminate (C). Most significantly, the Bush administration launched two enormously expensive wars in the Middle East—one in Afghanistan, one in Iraq. Eliminate (B). However, there was never another large-scale 9/11-style attack on U.S. soil, so select (A).

option_explanations.A: There has been no further large-scale 9/11-style attack on U.S. soil since 2001. The military and defense industry did not face another such attack — this is the exception.
option_explanations.B: The Bush administration did launch two prolonged Middle East wars — Afghanistan (2001) and Iraq (2003) — so this was a consequence, not the exception.
option_explanations.C: The Department of Homeland Security was established in 2002, consolidating about twenty agencies — so this was a consequence, not the exception.
option_explanations.D: Long-term investigations, including the 9/11 Commission, did examine the attacks' causes and funding — so this was a consequence, not the exception.
